This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is a bail application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Jagannath Prasad P.S. Case No.616 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No.194 of 2023 pending in the file of learned Additional District Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Berhampur, for commission of offences punishable U/Ss.363/366/376(2)(n)/376(3) of IPC r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act & Section 66E/67/67B of IT Act on the allegation of kidnapping the victim and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.

3. Heard Mr.S.S.Paikray, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.S.S.Pradhan, learned AGA and the father of the victim appearing in person virtually in the matter and perused the record.
4.

It is brought to the notice of the Court that co- accused-Jagannath Mahalik has already been granted bail by this Court, but the present petitioner is in custody since 21.10.2023 and in the meanwhile charge sheet has already been submitted.

The father of the victim, however, opposes the bail application of the petitioner on the ground that in the event of enlargement of the petitioner on bail, he would harass his family and would again take away the victim.

5. The material allegation appearing against the petitioner is that when the victim was cheated and sexually exploited by co-accused Surya Kumar Sahoo, the present petitioner who happens to be a friend of Surya Kumar Sahoo allured the victim and took her to Tiruchirappalli, Tamilnadu from Bhubaneswar and kept forcible physical relationship with her and subsequently left her there at Gouranga Patra vs State Of Orissa ...

Tiruchirappalli and thereafter, co- accused Jagannath Mahalik entered into the picture and he by alluring the victim again kept physical relationship with her as his wife by taking her to his house.

6. In the aforesaid backdrop of facts and after having considered the rival submissions and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of the offence, so also the accusation sought to be brought against the petitioner, which distinguishes him from co-accused released on bail and taking into the gravity of allegation against the petitioner, especially when there is allegation against him for not only keeping physical relationship with the victim, but also getting the objectional photograph of victim viral, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner at this stage, especially when the evidence of the victim is yet to be recorded.
7. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands rejected.
However, the petitioner is at liberty to renew his prayer for bail after examination of the victim in the trial.
8. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
9. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy) Judge kishore Signed by: KISHORE KUMAR SAHOO
